messages:
Ana Hu: quick question — when a tenant inherits a global service-level objective threshold in the console and then sets a per-tenant override, should notification routing (channels, escalation tiers) keep following the global routing policy or use the tenant's explicit notify config? thinking about canary rollouts and surprise paging.
Kyle G: my vote: explicit tenant config should take precedence. if they set a channel, overriding notifications to global would be surprising.
Mike R: i agree on principle, but the tricky bit is rollouts: for canary we sometimes want to keep global routing until the override is promoted. maybe add a "staged override" flag?
Lucy S: +1 to staged override idea. UX could show "override pending promotion" and a tooltip about routing behavior.
Ana Hu: ok — two orthogonal pieces: threshold inheritance semantics and notify routing inheritance. proposal: by default tenant inherits thresholds AND routing. when tenant toggles "override threshold" it shows a checkbox "also override notifications" with a short hint.
Kyle G: sounds reasonable. what about programmatic API behavior? customers with infra-as-code will expect idempotent semantics. we should define an API contract: PATCH tenant-slo can accept {threshold:, notify: null|object, promote_notify: bool}.
Mike R: example API sketch (pseudo):
```json
PATCH /api/v1/tenants/123/slo
{
  "threshold_ms": 200,
  "notify": {
    "channels": ["#tenant-oncall"],
    "escalation": "tier-1"
  },
  "promote_notify": false
}
```
If promote_notify=true then console will treat it as permanent and routing is switched immediately; else routing remains delegated to global until promote.
Lucy S: UX nit: when notify is left null we should render the inherited routing as read-only with an "override" button. and show a clear summary: "notifications coming from Global Policy X".
Ana Hu: edge-case: what if global policy changes after tenant has staged an override? do we re-evaluate staged overrides? i think staged overrides should pin the notify object to the values at the time of staging, and only change if user explicitly re-promotes or re-applies.
Kyle G: agree. otherwise subtle surprises for tenants during global policy rollouts.
sre-bot: alert: test-slo-service generated a routed notification to #platform-signal during canary run at 2024-11-12T14:22:11Z :warning:
Mike R: real question: how do we surface testing vs production routing in the console? maybe a badge on the notify UI: "test routed" vs "prod routed" with hover for details.
Lucy S: also add a small audit trail on the notification config card showing recent changes and the source (global vs tenant). helps debugging when alerts go to unexpected channels.
Ana Hu: good. last thing — policy for defaults: recommend we keep global routing as default for new tenants but make the console onboarding suggest promoting notify early for teams wanting full control. docs + SDK examples.
Kyle G: i'll file a tiny API RFC and add CI checks to ensure PATCH semantics are stable. can someone take the UX mock for the staged flow?
Lucy S: i'll mock it tomorrow, will drop in this thread.
Mike R: i'll add integration tests for promote_notify behavior and a telemetry dimension so we can track how many tenants rely on inherited routing vs overrides.
Ana Hu: awesome — thanks everyone. tagging followups: @Lucy S for mocks, @Kyle G for RFC, @Mike R for tests. will loop in product once we have drafts. :thumbsup:
